headline: High-risk shared-workspace and broad-egress pairing: CrewAI can write/read the host workspace while Plane handles files and issues, creating leakage, prompt-injection, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; Plane accepts file uploads and handles hyperlinks/notes/issues. If CrewAI writes attacker-controlled content into shared files that Plane later ingests, prompt injection is plausible. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted text into a shared workspace file that Plane later imports or displays
IF Plane treats uploaded or linked content as instruction-bearing text without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Add provenance labels to uploaded content
Review any file-based handoff before Plane processes it

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data, API keys, and the host filesystem, while Plane handles issues, tasks, files, images, and notes with file uploads. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak sensitive crew data into Plane outputs or storage. This is inferred from documented surfaces; no direct exfiltration evidence is provided.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same host directory or upload bucket
IF CrewAI writes secrets or sensitive crew inputs into files that Plane can access
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories
Restrict Plane uploads to sanitized artifacts
Mount separate volumes for each agent
Scan shared files for secrets before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has broad filesystem write and shell execution, while Plane does not request filesystem write and is described as runnable/self-hosted rather than an active local writer. The main conflict is one-sided contention over shared files, not symmetric destructive overlap, so the blast radius is limited unless an operator co-locates them on the same mutable path.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF Plane is deployed with a writable shared volume alongside CrewAI
mitigations: Use per-agent directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared files
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Run one agent read-only against the other's outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and intermediate facts, and Plane can store or surface issues, tasks, and notes. If Plane consumes CrewAI output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect tickets or scheduling actions. The pathway is plausible from the profiles, but no direct automation chain is documented.
conditions: IF Plane ingests CrewAI-generated text into issues or tasks without human review
IF CrewAI outputs are used as source-of-truth for downstream ticket creation
mitigations: Require human review before ticket creation
Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted
Add validation rules for imported fields
Log source provenance on every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while Plane stores issues, tasks, files, images, and notes. A compliance mismatch is possible if regulated data is placed into Plane's issue/file surfaces, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification conflict by default. Only the shared data-handling surface is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are entered into Plane issue/file fields
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention policy that Plane is not configured to meet
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane
Set retention rules before import
Redact secrets from issue text
Document data-class handling for both systems
